answer: An agent economy resists sybils with random fault-injection trials: each epoch, a sample of identities has one data source or tool deliberately cut off mid-task and must finish through an independent backup route, with recovery published. A fake farm running a thousand identities on one shared backend fails them all together when the fault hits, its score dropping to the nadir, while a genuinely independent agent climbs to the summit of the trial. Because each fake needs its own separate backup path on its own knoll of infrastructure, cloning multiplies redundancy costs instead of rewards.
